question: CTE welding instructor, 8 yrs industry. Cert?

answer.summary: Welding is a Career and Technical Education license area under LICN-010, but the passages do not make 8 years of industry experience alone sufficient for a license. Which certificate applies depends on the instructor's degree, whether they completed an educator preparation program, and whether they hold a North Carolina license already. Industry experience can also earn salary experience credit under LICN-006, which depends on the timing of their degree.

claims.text: Welding (Trade and Industrial Education - Welding) is a listed Career and Technical Education teaching license area.

An applicant with a high school diploma (or equivalent) or an associate's degree may be issued a teaching license in Career and Technical Education, provided the applicant meets all other requirements for the license classification sought.

Teacher license classifications include Initial Professional License, Continuing Professional License, Residency License, Limited License, Permit to Teach, Emergency License, International Faculty License, Lifetime License, and Provisional License. The classification depends on the applicant's qualifications.

A Permit to Teach may be requested by the employing PSU only if the applicant holds at least a bachelor's degree and has never been issued any other North Carolina professional educator license. It is valid until June 30 of the fiscal year requested and cannot be extended or renewed.

An Emergency License may be requested by the employing PSU only if the applicant holds a bachelor's degree with at least 18 credit hours of coursework relevant to the licensure area, has not completed a recognized EPP in that area, and does not qualify for a residency license. It is valid until June 30 and cannot be extended or renewed.

A Residency License requires the applicant to have completed at least 24 hours of coursework in the content area, or passed the applicable licensure examination for that content area, and to meet G.S. 115C-270.20(a)(5), which is not reproduced in the provided passages.

An Initial Professional License requires either completion of a recognized North Carolina EPP with EPP recommendation, completion of an EPP based outside North Carolina, or a clear out-of-state license with fewer than three years of licensed teaching experience. An IPL may be requested for an applicant who completed all EPP requirements but has not passed the licensure exam.

For salary purposes, non-teaching work experience may be credited only if it is relevant to the license area, was at least half-time (20 or more hours per week), was completed after age 18, did not include on-the-job training, was paid and documented, and is recommended by the PSU and accepted by DPI.

Non-teaching experience credit is one year for every two years of full-time relevant experience completed before the bachelor's degree, and one year for every year of full-time relevant experience completed after the bachelor's degree. Example for 8 years of qualifying experience: 4 years of credit if all were before the bachelor's degree, 8 years if all were after it, or a proportional mix if split. Partial years may be combined.

For Class V Career-Technical Trade and Industry Education licenses, one year of experience credit can be awarded for every year of full-time relevant non-teaching work experience after the individual has completed the required training and work experience to qualify for the provisional license.

Applicants must submit a license application with educational credentials, including official transcripts and documentation of EPP completion, and documentation of any applicable licensure examination performance.

The licensure examination for Welding is not listed in the LICN-003 testing table. The table footnote directs CTE licensure questions to the CTE Licensure Policy and Procedures Manual, which is not among the provided passages.
The in-state Initial Professional License application fee is $70.
citations: LICN-008 (North Carolina Department of Public Instruction Licensure Fees)

question: Preschool teacher with BS in child development wants to lateral-enter Birth-K. Eligible?

answer.summary: Eligibility depends on whether this person completed a recognized educator preparation program (EPP) in Birth-K, and on how many credit hours they have in that content area. Birth-K has no required licensure exam. The current routes are a residency license (needs 24 content-area hours or a passed exam), an emergency license, or a permit to teach. The current policies do not contain a 'lateral entry' pathway.

claims.text: A teacher license generally requires completion of an educator preparation program at the Bachelor's, Master's, Specialist, or Doctoral level.
Birth through Kindergarten is a teacher license area.
The licensure testing table lists no required test or score for the Birth through Kindergarten area.

A residency license may be requested by a PSU governing body for an applicant under its employment who meets G.S. 115C-270.20(a)(5) and has either completed at least 24 hours of coursework in the content area, or passed the applicable licensure examination requirements for that content area.

The policies do not state whether the no-exam status of Birth-K satisfies the 'passed the applicable licensure examination requirements' option in LICN-019 §1(a)(ii). The 24-hour option is the clearer path if the 24-hour count is met.
A residency license is a one-year license, renewable twice.

An emergency license may be requested for an applicant who holds a bachelor's degree with at least 18 credit hours of coursework relevant to the licensure area, has not completed a recognized EPP in that area, and does not qualify for a residency license. It is valid until June 30 of the fiscal year requested and cannot be extended or renewed.

A permit to teach may be requested by a PSU for an applicant who holds at least a bachelor's degree and has never been issued any other North Carolina professional educator license. It is valid until June 30 of the fiscal year requested and cannot be extended or renewed.

The lateral entry license under G.S. 115C-297 was repealed by S.L. 2017-189. The policies allow residency or limited licenses for prior lateral entry license holders only, so they do not apply unless this person previously held one.
The policies provided do not say whether a bachelor's degree in child development counts as an EPP, or whether its coursework counts toward the 24-hour or 18-hour thresholds.

question: Teacher on a limited license for a special subject, 3 years in. Can they keep renewing it?

answer.summary: A limited license for a teaching area can be renewed under LICN-023 if the employing PSU files a supervisor-and-superintendent affidavit and the teacher meets EVAAS growth where data exists. Confirm current PSU employment, effectiveness, and EVAAS data availability before advising; the passages do not address a renewal cap or how a limited license converts to a CPL.

claims.text: A limited license is a three-year renewable license issued to someone who completed an EPP but has not satisfied the applicable licensure examination requirements.

A limited license may only be issued for teaching license areas. Special Subjects such as Art, Music, and Health and Physical Education are teaching license areas, so a special-subject teacher is eligible in principle.

To renew, the PSU governing body employing the licensee must submit an affidavit signed by the licensee's supervising principal and the local superintendent (or equivalent chief executive officer). It must attest that the licensee is currently employed by the PSU, is an effective teacher, and that the PSU will encourage the licensee to pursue a CPL.

The licensee must also demonstrate meeting or exceeding expected growth on EVAAS, where such data is available. If there is more than one year of growth data, DPI averages it. Only data from the years since the limited license was first issued or its most recent renewal counts, and DPI does not consider 2019-2020 or 2020-2021 EVAAS data.

Portability is limited: a limited license may not transfer from one PSU to another, except for military service members and spouses covered by LICN-028. A teacher who changes employers would therefore not carry the license with them.

Under LICN-023 §1(b), a lateral entry license holder who has not passed the exam may qualify for a limited license under a different set of conditions, including a superintendent and principal affidavit, if the person is currently employed by the PSU. That provision applies only to legacy lateral entry holders, not to general limited license renewal.

For a CPL, a teacher must hold an IPL or residency license, satisfy exam requirements, and have at least three years of licensed teaching experience. The passages do not say how a limited license holder converts to a CPL, so the LICN-024 pathway does not directly apply to a limited license holder.

questions_for_user: Is the teacher currently employed by the PSU that would submit the renewal affidavit?
Will the supervising principal and local superintendent attest that the teacher is an effective teacher?
Does the teacher have EVAAS growth data for the years since the limited license was first issued or last renewed? EVAAS data may not exist for every special subject.
Is the "3 years in" three years of teaching experience, or three years on the limited license? The limited license term is three years.
Has the teacher previously renewed this limited license, and does the PSU intend to encourage a CPL pathway?
not_covered: Whether there is a maximum number of times a limited license can be renewed.
What happens if the teacher has no EVAAS growth data for a special subject. LICN-023 §2(b) applies only "where such data is available" and does not say what applies otherwise.
How a limited license converts to an IPL or CPL, and whether LICN-024 applies to limited license holders.
Whether the teacher's special subject has a required licensure exam, which affects the path to a standard license (see LICN-003).

metrics.judge_rationale: The answer reaches the key's needs_more_info verdict and correctly states the affidavit, EVAAS averaging with excluded years, and portability rules, all supported by the cited text. It omits the LICN-028 §6 servicemember detail and the rule that added license areas are not allowed, and its claim about LICN-024 not applying is an inference rather than stated text.

question: how long does DPI take to process a license application after its submitted online

answer.summary: The LICN policies provided do not state how long DPI takes to process a license application, and they do not address online submission. claims.text: DPI must issue a license once the applicant submits a complete license application. An application is complete when the applicant has submitted all required information, documentation, and credentials under LICN-004, paid the application fee under LICN-008, and, if applicable, been cleared from any Superintendent investigation under LICN-007.
A complete application for a licensure service other than license renewal should be submitted to DPI by April 15 of a given fiscal year to guarantee processing before the end of that fiscal year.

If a complete application is submitted after April 15 and DPI does not approve it before the fiscal year ends, the employing public school unit may not use State or federal funds to pay the applicant's salary for the fiscal year in which the application was submitted.
The fiscal year runs July 1 through June 30.

The application must include the applicant's identifying information, educational credentials, disclosures, proof of any out-of-state license, and documentation of licensure exam performance, and the applicant must pay the fee set in LICN-008.

question: Candidate has an MLS from a university, applying for NC media coordinator. Is that enough?

answer.summary: An MLS at the master's level matches the degree level required for a student services personnel license, but the passages do not treat the degree alone as sufficient: it must come from a recognized educator preparation program, and the candidate must meet the Praxis 5312 requirement (or receive an initial license until they do). Confirm the EPP status and exam status before deciding.

claims.text: Media Coordinator is one of the student services personnel license classifications.

To qualify for a student services personnel license, an applicant must have completed an educator preparation program at the master's (M), specialist (S), or doctoral (D) level. A master's-level degree therefore meets the level requirement only if it was completed through an EPP.

The passages do not say whether a university MLS program is an EPP. An EPP must be recognized by the State Board of Education, or by the equivalent licensing authority in the jurisdiction where the EPP has its principal place of business. Having a master's degree alone does not establish this.
The applicant's highest degree level is the level for which they are eligible; the license is issued at the highest degree level at which the applicant completed an EPP.
Media Coordinator requires the Praxis 5312 test with a required score of 154.

Student services personnel must satisfy applicable licensure exam requirements before or during the third year of licensure, and must attempt the exam at least once during the first year. If the exam is passed before applying, the applicant receives a continuing professional license; if not, but otherwise qualified, the applicant receives an initial professional license.
The application must include official transcripts for the degree and documentation, signed by an EPP official, that the applicant completed an EPP for the license classification sought.

If the MLS was completed outside North Carolina, the applicant is an out-of-state applicant. Out-of-state applicants with an EPP based outside NC qualify for an initial professional license under LICN-020 §1(b) or LICN-025, and the policies for out-of-state exam results apply.

question: Teacher has a CPL in science and wants to add math 6-9. How many credits?

answer.summary: A CPL holder can add Middle Grades Mathematics (6-9) either by passing the required licensure exam or by completing 24 credit hours of higher-education coursework in math with a grade of C or better in each course. The policies do not set a separate credit count beyond the 24 hours, so the answer is 24 credit hours or zero if the exam is passed instead.

claims.text: Middle Grades Mathematics (Grades 6-9) is a valid teaching license area under the teacher license classifications.
An applicant may add a new license area to an existing CPL, subject to LICN-013.

To add a teaching area, the applicant must either satisfy the applicable licensure examination requirements for that area, or complete 24 credit hours of coursework from an institution of higher education in the license area with a grade of C or better in each course.

Calculation: the coursework route requires 24 credit hours total. The exam route requires 0 additional credit hours but requires passing the exam. Any credits already earned count only if they meet the 24-hour, grade-C-or-better, in-area requirements, which the policy does not explicitly address.
The Middle Grades Mathematics exam is Praxis 5164 with a required score of 157 (licensure code 78200).
Elementary Education and Exceptional Children: General Curriculum cannot be added through coursework alone. Middle Grades Mathematics is not on that list, so the coursework route is available for it.
The add-area fee is $60 for either 'Add Area by Test or 24 Sem. Hrs.' or 'Add Area by Program Completion' when opened by an individual educator.

question: What's the current salary step for a teacher with a CPL and 12 years experience at Union County?

answer.summary: The policies provided do not contain the State Salary Schedule or any salary step amounts, so I cannot give a step for this teacher or for Union County. The passages do show that experience credit, which drives the step, is earned under the experience rules in LICN-006, and the analyst would need the schedule itself and the teacher's credited experience and degree level to finish the calculation.

claims.text: Salary for a North Carolina public school employee is determined by the amount of creditable experience the individual has.

The passages define the State Salary Schedule as the schedule for teachers and other public school personnel administered by the State Board of Education, but they do not set out the schedule's steps or dollar amounts.

One year of experience credit is earned for full-time work in a school unit of at least six calendar months within one fiscal year (July 1 through June 30). Twelve years of credit therefore requires twelve such fiscal years, unless partial years are combined under the combination rule.
Part-time work counts toward experience credit only if it is at least 15 hours per week, and two years of part-time work can combine into one year if it equals six months of full-time experience.

Substitute teaching, tutoring, and clerical paraprofessional service do not count as professional educator experience credit, and experience credit is not awarded during leave of absence except as required by workers' compensation and USERRA.

Each license states the applicant's degree level, based on the highest degree issued by an educator preparation program, and an applicant is only eligible for a license at the highest degree level completed. Salary depends on the degree level as well as experience, so the degree level is needed.

Graduate degree salary pay is available only if the Department of Public Instruction approves it under the criteria in LICN-006 Section V, which include the degree being directly related to the educator's license area.

The policies do not address Union County's local salary supplements or local pay scales. A PSU may set additional requirements for its employees, but the policies do not say anything about local salary.

question: RL teacher, passed Praxis, 2 yrs in. Upgrade to IPL?

answer.summary: Passing the Praxis does not by itself convert a residency license to an IPL. Conversion requires meeting the IPL requirements in LICN-020, including completion of a recognized EPP and an EPP recommendation, and it must happen by June 30 of the residency license's third year to take effect July 1. Confirm the EPP status, the license start date, and whether the 'two years' means time on the residency license or time teaching.

claims.text: A residency license may be converted to an IPL or CPL only if the applicant meets the IPL requirements in LICN-020 or the CPL requirements in LICN-024, and is recommended by the EPP that prepared the licensee.

Under LICN-020 §1(a), an applicant qualifies for an IPL by completing a recognized North Carolina EPP and being recommended by that EPP for the requested license. Alternative routes are an EPP completed outside North Carolina (§1(b)) or an out-of-state clear license with fewer than three years of licensed teaching experience (§1(c)).

Under LICN-020 §2, a PSU may request an IPL for an applicant who has completed all EPP academic, field, and clinical requirements but has not satisfied the licensure examination requirements, and in that case the EPP recommendation is not required. The passages do not say that passing the Praxis converts a residency license to an IPL.

Residency license renewal requires that the applicant be enrolled in a recognized EPP, which suggests the EPP may not yet have finished. Completion of the EPP is a condition of IPL eligibility under LICN-020 §1(a).

Passing the required licensure examination is a CPL requirement. A CPL requires an IPL or residency license, satisfied exam requirements before or during the third year, and at least three years of licensed teaching experience, plus a Beginning Teacher Support Program unless an exception applies. At two years in, the three-year experience requirement is not yet met.

question: International applicant, bachelor's from India, 6 years teaching math there, wants NC license. Next steps?

claims.text: Under LICN-001 §2(r), an out-of-state applicant is one who completed an educator or administrator preparation program with a principal place of business outside North Carolina, and this includes international preparation programs. The applicant falls in this category.

An out-of-state applicant with more than three years of licensed professional educator experience may qualify for a continuing professional license under LICN-025 §2. An out-of-state applicant with fewer than three years may qualify for an initial professional license under LICN-025 §1(a). A six-year applicant falls under §2 only if all six years were licensed teaching experience.

Only licensed experience counts for this threshold. The policies measure 'licensed professional educator experience' and 'licensed teaching experience,' so unlicensed teaching in India would not count toward the three-year threshold.

To qualify for the CPL under LICN-025 §2, the applicant must meet both (a) and (b). Criterion (a) requires a clear license from the foreign jurisdiction, meaning one that is in good standing, renewable by the issuing authority, not revoked or disciplined, not under pending unprofessional-conduct investigation, and not surrendered under investigation. Criterion (b) requires either a National Board for Professional Teaching Standards certification or substantially similar licensure requirements.

'Substantially similar' under LICN-025 §2(b) requires that the other jurisdiction required, at minimum, completion of an educator preparation program recognized by the state where the EPP is located, and a passing score on an out-of-state exam for each license area sought. If the applicant lacks NBPTS certification, both of these must be shown.

For the math license area, the applicant would need the North Carolina Mathematics test, Praxis 5165 with a required score of 159, unless an out-of-state exam is used. Under LICN-025 §3, out-of-state exam results must be presented at initial licensure, and an out-of-state applicant may not use out-of-state exam results to convert an IPL to a CPL.

Mathematics is a recognized license area at the Middle Grades (6-9) and Secondary (9-12) levels, so the applicant's subject area can be licensed. The grade band must be confirmed before matching the license area.

An applicant is eligible only for a license at the highest degree level at which the applicant completed an EPP. A bachelor's degree licenses at the A-Level, and LICN-010 §2 requires completion of an educator preparation program at one of the listed levels. Whether the Indian bachelor's was an educator preparation program is not stated.

Under LICN-001 §3(d), an EPP must be recognized by the SBE or by the equivalent licensing authority in the jurisdiction where the EPP is located. The policies do not say whether any Indian program or authority is recognized.

An applicant from outside North Carolina who has at least three years of licensed teaching experience outside North Carolina is exempt from the Beginning Teacher Support Program requirement for a CPL. The policy text applies this exemption to the NC CPL pathway in LICN-024 §1(d)(i); the policies do not clearly apply it to the LICN-025 §2 pathway.

Out-of-state exam scores must be presented at the time of initial licensure in North Carolina. Under LICN-025 §4, an applicant may later add a teaching area based on an out-of-state exam only if the evidence is submitted at the time of initial application.

The application requires official transcripts for the degree, documentation of EPP completion, disclosure of any prior license suspension or revocation and criminal history, proof of any current valid license from another state if applicable, and documentation of licensure exam performance. The application fee for an out-of-state initial professional license is $100 when opened by the individual.

A complete application must be submitted, and fees paid, before DPI issues a license. An application for a licensure service other than renewal must be submitted by April 15 to guarantee processing before the end of the fiscal year.

Which rules applied to a 2025 application, since the provided policies are current versions effective 2026.

incorrect_statements: LICN-003 covers CTE only through a footnote referring to a separate manual; the cited LICN-003 §5 table actually lists Career-Technical Education test requirements for Family & Consumer Sciences, Marketing, Technology, Business, and Computer Science & IT.
metrics.judge_rationale: The bottom line matches the key: the policies do not address industry credentials or their validity, so the 2016 credential cannot be assessed and the manual and 2025 rules must be checked. However, the answer wrongly says LICN-003 covers CTE only by footnote, contradicting its own cited testing table, and it omits the high school diploma pathway, salary experience credit, and Class V provisional license points.
